publication_endpoint: independent temporal test of whether movement stabilises experienced microhabitat state relative to event-matched local availability
seed_system: King Rail / Gulf Coast marsh EOG anomaly
first_independent_system: western Lake Erie King Rail telemetry and paired microhabitat surveys
core_hypothesis: resident birds can maintain fidelity to environmental state by moving within familiar geographic space as hydrological conditions change

primary_estimands.SRI: 1 - temporal variance of used water depth / median matched-random pseudo-trajectory variance
primary_estimands.environmental_displacement: change in environmental state between consecutive used locations

primary_predictions: used water-depth state varies less through time than event-matched local availability
real geographic movement can occur while environmental-state displacement remains lower than matched pseudo-trajectories
individual state-fidelity signal is not driven by one bird
later_extension: full hydrological-portfolio/HPI buffering only if repeated spatial habitat surfaces can be reconstructed
falsification: used-state variance is not lower than matched availability
environmental displacement is indistinguishable from pseudo-trajectories
state fidelity appears only after post-hoc tuning of a preferred water-depth window
one individual drives the aggregate result
eog_role: discovery clue that geographic propagation was a poor ecological representation
replication_unit: individual bird; n=10 stabilized-home-range individuals in Lake Erie seed

published_design_audit.intended_matching: 1 used + 2 random-direction points 75 m away within 72 h
published_design_audit.primary_inference: within-individual matched pseudo-trajectories, then individual-level synthesis
published_design_audit.pseudoreplication_rule: do not use 607 point records as independent biological replicates
